speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Lee and Prime Minister Mahathir had very candid discussions and they both reaffirmed our mutual commitment to maintaining a positive and constructive bilateral relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I will now provide an update on four key areas: the maritime boundaries, air, water, and land connectivity issues.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Malaysian Government vessels are no longer anchored in the area.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The next step is for both countries to start negotiations on the maritime boundary, and we will do so through the committee that is co-chaired by the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Secretary General of the Malaysian Foreign Affairs Ministry.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On water, our position has remained clear, consistent and unchanged.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At the Retreat, we reiterated that Malaysia has lost the right to review the price of water under the 1962 Water Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Neither country can unilaterally change the terms of this Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The 1962 Water Agreement is enshrined in the 1965 Separation Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is, therefore, a fundamental founding document for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our Attorneys-General are having further discussions on the differing legal positions of both sides on the right to review the price of water under the 1962 Water Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Whilst Malaysia is apparently most concerned about the price of raw water, this issue cannot be viewed in isolation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: First, if there is any revision in the price of raw water, it is obvious that the price of treated water that Singapore sells to Johor will also have to be revised.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Second, at the Retreat, Prime Minister Lee highlighted Singapore’s grave concerns about the multiple pollution incidents which have affected the Johor River and the long-term yield of the Johor River.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members of the House would be aware, and I think Minister Masagos Zulkifli reminded us of this over the last two days, of the recent case of ammonia pollution in the Johor River on 4 April 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is the seventh pollution incident in the Johor River since 2017 which led to a shutdown of our Waterworks.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Further, Johor has built at least two water treatment plants upstream of the Public Utilities Board's (PUB’s) Johor River Waterworks, and we also note that the future demands for water in Johor will increase.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These two Malaysian plants, combined with our Johor River Waterworks, are currently drawing more water from the Johor River than it can yield on a sustainable basis.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These issues, if not addressed, will compromise Singapore’s right to extract our full 250 million gallons per day (mgd) entitlement of water under the 1962 Water Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They will also affect the water supply for Johor’s own growing needs, and action needs to be taken expeditiously to avoid a potentially more intractable issue in the future.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is a problem which is clear and present and we can see it looming.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both sides have noted Singapore and Malaysia’s mutual interest in identifying appropriate and timely measures, including additional schemes, to increase the yield of the Johor River, and to safeguard its environmental conditions, and to safeguard, in particular, the quality of the water.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Officials from both countries will follow up on this.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The two Foreign Ministers have also been tasked to follow up on the water issues that were raised at the Retreat.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The ILS procedures will be replaced with GPS-based instrument approach procedures.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The technical agencies from both countries are currently engaged in discussions with a view to implementing the GPS-based instrument approach procedures soon for both the northern and southern approaches.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At the Retreat, Malaysia reiterated its intention to review the existing arrangements for air traffic services provision over southern Peninsular Malaysia pursuant to the 1974 Operational Letter of Agreement that was signed by Malaysia and Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is very important to note that this 1974 Operational Letter of Agreement, in fact, operationalises the decisions that were reached at the 1973 Asia-Pacific Regional Air Navigation Meeting held under the auspices of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This decision sets out the recommendations that were agreed to by both Singapore and Malaysia, as well as other regional states, and was subsequently approved by the ICAO Council.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Thus, any review of the existing airspace arrangements should take into account both countries’ needs and interests, as well as the interests of other stakeholders, including the airlines and ICAO.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Any proposal to change the current arrangements must also be in accordance with ICAO standards, processes and procedures, and the 1973 decision I mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our utmost priority must be to achieve the highest standards of safety and efficiency in civil aviation operations, given that the airspace arrangements in our region are very complex and will only get more complex in the future as air traffic continues to grow.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Discussions on the review of the 1974 Operational Letter of Agreement will involve consultations with many regional and global stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore will discuss these matters with Malaysia in good faith and in the spirit of bilateral cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both sides are currently working out the details of the Supplemental Agreement to effect this proposed suspension.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both Prime Ministers also discussed the issue of congestion at the Causeway and Second Link.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both Prime Ministers agreed to explore initiatives, including the use of new technology, for enhanced security and checkpoint efficiency.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Lee also shared Singapore’s plans to upgrade the Woodlands Checkpoint to meet growing traffic needs, and to ensure that immigration clearance remains secure.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore believes that the RTS Link and the HSR Projects are mutually beneficial projects that will significantly ease congestion, facilitate business and tourism, and bring the people of Malaysia and Singapore closer together.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Malaysia wants to review these projects, and we have agreed for this review to be done in the spirit of bilateral cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: What is important is that we continue to keep the channels of communication open; we discuss these issues in a calm and constructive way, on the basis of equality and mutual respect; we honour our international agreements fully, and we find amicable win-win solutions in accordance with international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I believe both sides have demonstrated, at the Leaders’ Retreat, a commitment to manage some of the recent bilateral issues to ensure that we protect our broader, multifaceted relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are now on a more stable footing.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But there is still much work to be done, and there are also new areas of cooperation which we hope to explore together.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore is ready and willing to cooperate with Malaysia in the spirit of goodwill and neighbourliness.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But this is more of a subjective question.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Does the Minister feel that good relationships have also been built at all levels, including at the working level where all the implementation will take place?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Because the Malaysian government is very large and many of the Ministers are new and I think at the working level, the government-to-government level, it will be good to have relationships as well.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I am wondering if this is the first step to building relationships at a deeper level.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I think at the people-to-people level, given our history and the fact that most of us have relatives on both sides of the Causeway, I believe Singaporeans and Malaysians want good relations between our two states.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Having said that, I think it is just as important for the Civil Service, the officials, the Members of Parliament from all parties, and Ministers and obviously the Prime Ministers, to also continue to engage one another, look for areas where we can cooperate constructively, understand each other's concerns and anxieties and then try to make progress.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I want to encourage more interaction between the civil servants and Parliamentarians.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I would encourage all of you to do so when the opportunities arise.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My question pertains to the comments made by the Minister with regard to water and, particularly, the right of Singapore under the 1962 Water Agreement to draw up to 250 mgd from Johor.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Minister said that, in future, it would appear that there would be a risk that we would not be able to draw that amount, given that Johor's own needs are likely to grow.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I ask the Minister, prior to today, for example, have there been situations where we have not been able to draw the 250 mgd, apart from those incidents where the waterworks had to be shut down?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, this should focus their minds on protecting the environmental standards and the quality of the water in the rivers.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And again, as a former Minister in charge of water, I need to remind Members if you walk outside Parliament, you will realise that every drain, every longkang in the city, flows into Marina Bay.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And we drink the water from Marina Bay, after appropriate treatment.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The challenge in maintaining that quality of assured water supply is not just a technical challenge.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It means having strict laws against littering, against pollution, strict and careful long-term planning on zoning, on what type of economic activities are allowed in the water catchment area.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And in fact, this has been a key critical ingredient for Singapore's success in water management.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The fact is, actually, the same approach is needed in Johor.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I do not want to belabour this point because, to be fair, the authorities in Johor are aware of this, and within their own limits, they are trying to address it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I do want to add one more point that, actually, PUB has an excellent relationship with the water agencies in Johor.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There is no problem at the technical level.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Speaker, just to follow up on the Minister's last point.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Would Singapore consider providing material or technical assistance to Malaysia on a bilateral basis to safeguard the Johor River watershed?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Is it something we are prepared to do?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Actually, Singapore and Malaysia have been working on this for a very long time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would have to remind everyone, including the Malaysians, that Singapore paid for it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We paid for its construction, we paid compensation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, there should be no question about our willingness to engage and assist on a technical level in order to further projects which ultimately have win-win consequences for both Johor and Singapore in the long term.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I say all this so that I hope the Malaysian people appreciate that Singapore has been a constructive, helpful, reliable and honest partner.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And actually the more important fundamental point – if you cut across all the political polemic which you often hear – the fact is that the Water Agreements – the 1961 Agreement which has expired and the 1962 Agreement which is still in effect – actually have brought enormous benefit to the people of both Malaysia and Singapore.
